segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
[... Qutb] al-Dīn Muhammad, the lord of Sinjār, and the lord of Mardin,
and they went to take Mesopotamia away from the house of al-ʿĀdil.
And when they reached Ra's al-'Ayn,
sickness fell upon them,
because it was summer.
And also the son of al-ʿĀdil, whose name was al-Malik al-Fā'iz, was in Harran,
and he sent to Nūr al-Dīn and sought peace from him.
Then Nūr al-Dīn,
because he heard of the reconciliation that had taken place between al-Afdal and al-Zāhir and the house of al-ʿĀdil, their uncle,
and also because of the sickness,
consented to peace.
And they swore oaths to him,
and he swore {OCR?} to them.
And he left and returned to Mosul,
and those who were with him, each one to his own place.
And in that same year, while Mu'izz al-Dīn Qaysar-Shāh was reigning in Melitene,
his brother Rukn al-Dīn Sulaymān, son of Qilij Arslān, went against him.
And he attacked it,
and took it from him in the month of June of the year 1511,
1511 of the Greeks [1200 AD].
And that Mu'izz al-Dīn Qaysar-Shāh fled from before his brother to al-Malik al-ʿĀdil, his father-in-law.
And al-ʿĀdil sent and had him live in Edessa, while giving him allowances.
And from there that Rukn al-Dīn went to Erzurum.
And there was in it the son of Malik Muhammad ibn Saltuq,
for they were an ancient house,
and had been reigning over Erzurum for a long time.
And when that lord of it went out to Rukn al-Dīn in the manner of love and humility,
he seized him and imprisoned him with him,
and he took the city.
And he also took Iconium from Ghiyāth al-Dīn Kaykhusraw, his brother.
And that Ghiyāth al-Dīn fled to Syria,
and came to al-Malik al-Zāhir, the lord of Aleppo,
and informed him of the matter, (hoping) that perhaps he might help him.
And when he saw no help from him,
he departed from him and disguised himself.
And he moved from place to place,
until he arrived at Constantinople.
And the king of the Greeks honored him exceedingly,
and gave him for a wife the daughter of one of the great patricians.
And he remained there until the Franks took Constantinople,
as we are going to show.
And when the Franks took control of Constantinople,
that Ghiyāth al-Dīn fled to his father-in-law,
who was the lord of one of the fortresses.
And his father-in-law received him and said to him:
